title: Multiplexing, spread spectrum and switching
subtitle: How many conversations share one wire, and how a call finds its way across a network.

fdm.title: Frequency-division and time-division multiplexing
fdm.body: Multiplexing combines many signals onto one medium. FDM gives each signal its own frequency band (radio stations, cable TV) with guard bands between them. TDM gives each signal the whole channel for a short time slot in rotation: synchronous TDM wastes slots when a source is idle; statistical TDM allocates slots on demand. WDM is FDM for light: each colour carries a channel on one fibre.
fdm.steps: A T1 line multiplexes 24 voice channels, each 64 kb/s, plus 8 kb/s framing. 24 × 64 = 1536 kb/s; add 8 kb/s framing.

dsl.title: ADSL and xDSL
dsl.body: ADSL uses the copper pair in three frequency bands: voice (0–4 kHz), upstream and a much wider downstream band — asymmetric because home users download more than they upload. It uses discrete multitone: the band is split into 4 kHz sub-channels, each modulated with as many bits as its own signal-to-noise ratio allows. Speed falls with distance from the exchange.

ss.title: Spread spectrum and CDMA
ss.body: Spread spectrum deliberately uses far more bandwidth than needed: FHSS hops the carrier among frequencies in a pseudo-random sequence; DSSS multiplies each bit by a fast chipping code. In CDMA every user has a different orthogonal code and all transmit at once on the same band; the receiver recovers one user by correlating with that user’s code — the others average to zero.
ss.steps: Two users with orthogonal codes c₁ = (+1 +1 +1 +1) and c₂ = (+1 −1 +1 −1). User 1 sends bit +1, user 2 sends bit −1. The channel carries the sum: c₁ − c₂ = (0, 2, 0, 2). Receiver for user 1 correlates with c₁ and divides by 4. For user 2: correlate with c₂ = (0·1 + 2·(−1) + 0·1 + 2·(−1))/4 = −1 ✓.

sw.title: Circuit, message and packet switching
sw.body: Circuit switching reserves a path for the whole call (telephone): guaranteed rate, set-up delay, idle capacity wasted. Message switching stores and forwards whole messages. Packet switching cuts data into packets routed separately: efficient for bursty traffic, variable delay. Two flavours: datagram (each packet routed independently, may arrive out of order) and virtual circuit (a path is set up first; packets follow it in order).
sw.steps: Send a 1.5 MB file over 4 hops of 1 Mb/s each, propagation ignored. Packet size 1500 B, 1000 packets. Store-and-forward message switching: each hop retransmits the whole file: 4 × 12 s = 48 s. Packet switching pipelines: first hop takes 12 s, then the last packet needs 3 more hop-times of 12 ms: ≈ 12.04 s.

dev.title: Switching devices
dev.body: A crossbar switch connects any input to any output with n² crosspoints; multistage (Banyan/Clos) networks use fewer small switches at the price of possible blocking. A packet switch adds buffers to hold packets contending for the same output.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• FDM splits frequency, TDM splits time, WDM splits colour, CDMA splits by code.
  • Circuit switching reserves; packet switching shares.
